data.name: Gopaal
data.long_meaning: Gopaal is a name derived from the Sanskrit language, meaning 'Protector of Cows and People'. In Hindu mythology, Lord Gopaal is an avatar of Lord Vishnu who is often depicted as a cowherd. He is believed to be the protector and preserver of all beings, and is revered for his compassionate and nurturing nature.

In Hindu philosophy, he represents spiritual nourishment and self-sacrifice, as He is the Protector of all creatures – both bovine and human. Hindu devotional texts often describe Lord Gopaal as a caregiver and healer, invoking feelings of humility, devotion, and surrender. He is a reminder of the divine grace and compassion that dwells within us and is embodied in the form of a nurturing, protective deity.
